senses.definition: To traverse a slope or contour, either upwards (ascending) or downwards (descending).
senses.example: after I had found (the goats') haunts a little, I laid wait in this manner for them: I observed if they saw me in the valleys, though they were upon the rocks, they would run away, as in a terrible fright; but if they were feeding in the valleys, and I was upon the rocks, they took no notice of me; from whence I concluded that, by the position of their optics, their sight was so directed downward that they did not readily see objects that were above them; so afterwards I took this method - I always climbed the rocks first, to get above them, and then had frequently a fair mark.

senses.definition: (literally or figuratively): To ascend; rise; to go up.
senses.example: Black vapours climb aloft, and cloud the day.

senses.definition: To mount; to move upwards on.
To scale; to get to the top of something.
senses.example: He is a curly-haired schoolboy barely in his teens, but 13-year-old Jordan Romero from California has become the youngest person to climb Mount Everest.

senses.definition: To enter, mount or otherwise assume a position in or on a conveyance.
senses.example: He climbed into the passenger-seat of the car.

senses.definition: To move (especially up and down something) by gripping with the hands and using the feet.
senses.example: My legs were so stiff and my arms so sore that this morning I could barely climb out of bed.

senses.definition: To practise the sport of climbing.

senses.example: The defender climbed majestically at the near post to convert Johnson's corner.

senses.definition: (botany) Of plants, to grow upwards by clinging to something.

senses.example: Make sure that you keep checking to see that everything remains safe throughout the climb.

senses.definition: The act of getting to somewhere more elevated.
senses.example: The Mur de Péguère is a savage little climb, its last four kilometres a narrow tunnel of trees and excited spectators urging on the straining riders.
After a decade of prosperity, millions of Asians are likely to be pushed into poverty, and the climb out of poverty will stall for millions of others.
